translation_notes: prefixes: OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SKOS->skos, XSD->xsd from the draft are narrowed to owl/rdfs only: the region's own body never uses RDF.* (rdf:type is written with the Turtle `a` shorthand, not a prefixed name) or SKOS.*/XSD.* at all -- an unused @prefix is noise (already noted for a prior trav_navigation region in this same batch).

the region chains THREE separate `.subjects()`/`.objects()` calls: candidate classes (`graph.subjects(RDF.type, OWL.Class)`), then per-candidate parents (`graph.objects(class_uri, RDFS.subClassOf)`) and children (`graph.subjects(RDFS.subClassOf, class_uri)`). Unlike a prior trav_navigation region in this same repository family, these do NOT fuse into one `m{ }` join: the control flow between them is `if not parents and not children`, a conjunction of two NEGATED existence checks, and `m{ }` has no FILTER/NOT EXISTS to express a negation at all. Each step gets its own most-specific `m{ }` instead: `m{ ?class_uri a owl:Class }` (arity 1, terms), `m{ {class_uri} rdfs:subClassOf ?p }` (arity 1, terms -- replaces `.objects()`), `m{ ?s rdfs:subClassOf {class_uri} }` (arity 1, terms -- replaces `.subjects()`). This is the counter-example to 'trav_navigation always means fuse into one join': fusion is only valid for a positive AND-chain, and this region's gate is a NOR.

`isinstance(class_uri, URIRef)` (excluding a blank-node class) cannot move into any pattern -- `m{ }` has no term-kind filter -- and stays exactly where Python would run it, now applied to a solution from `m{ }` instead of from `graph.subjects()`. Same for `class_uri == owl_thing` and `p != owl_thing`: ordinary Python term comparison, unaffected by the switch to islands.
`owl_thing = OWL.Thing` becomes `owl_thing = owl:Thing`: a prefixed name with no variable in it, resolved immediately, exactly the case the reference calls out as needing no bindings at all.

`self._get_label`/`self._get_local_name` are plain method calls, untouched by the translation; `self` is a shared, stateless context_shim.OntologyLinter instance reused for every call on both sides (see driver.py), matching the same pattern already used for a `self`-receiver in this batch's other final region.

`_check_orphan_class` is `async def` with no `await` in its own body (it is declared async only for consistency with its sibling `_check_*` methods, which the real `OntologyLinter.lint()` awaits); `run_check_orphan_class`, added identically to both files and excluded from surface metrics like a context shim, drives the coroutine synchronously since the harness calls its entry point with no event loop.

fixture.ttl carries three orphans -- a plain one, one with an rdfs:label (exercising `_get_label`'s non-None branch) and one whose only rdfs:subClassOf is owl:Thing (proving the 'excluding owl:Thing' filter on parents actually fires) -- plus owl:Thing itself typed owl:Class (would otherwise qualify as an orphan; proves the identity skip), a class with a real parent, that parent (which is thereby disqualified by having a child), a blank-node-typed owl:Class (proves the isinstance guard), and a resource not typed owl:Class at all (never even a candidate). A second driver call passes an empty graph for the zero-solution case (verified directly: exactly the 3 expected orphans and no more, see driver run).
